outcome: Maybe, leaning yes, but not today. She read the email to the end, tapped the link, found the page factual and free of any ask for money, and liked that the reply is optional and can be off the record. She stopped on the phone at screen 5 when she saw a money balance (£5.00, 'This page 0.5p of 5p') and came back to About only out of duty; About's own 'Gap' paragraph and the 'not independent of RiskMandate' line made her decide the 15 minutes is probably a RiskMandate conversation as well as an interview. At her desk she forwarded the link to her co-founder with 'check this, maybe reply with two lines on how the product works, no call yet'. She did not reply on Friday.

steps.see: Subject 'A ChatPlace no PrompTugal.news, antes da Web Summit'. No 'Olá', it opens straight with 'Antes da Web Summit Lisboa, escrevemos uma página sobre a ChatPlace'. A link. 'Há uma secção ainda vazia: os fluxos'. 'Responder é opcional. Se preferirem conversar sem publicar, conversamos.' Signed 'Dinis Cruz, Editor, PrompTugal.news (powered by RiskMandate)'. Last line: 'Escrito por um agente de IA, revisto e enviado por mim.'
steps.think: No greeting feels cold, like a bulk send. But it is short, in Portuguese, it says the page already exists and nobody asks me for money. 'Responder é opcional' and 'sem publicar' lower my guard. 'powered by RiskMandate' raises it again: who is RiskMandate and why is a newsroom powered by a company? 'Escrito por um agente de IA' is honest; I respect that more than a fake personal note.
steps.question: What is RiskMandate, and is the 15 minutes an interview or a demo?
steps.confusion: The email says 'mandato: mapear o universo da IA em Portugal' and then 'powered by RiskMandate', and also asks about 'mandate' in the three questions: the word mandate means three different things in one email.
steps.act: Tap the link, because the page is about my company and I want to see what they wrote before I decide anything.

steps.see: Masthead 'PrompTugal.news', 'Powered by RiskMandate' with a logo, then in the nav a pill '£5.00' and 'Vault'. 'ChatPlace' big, 'Based in Portugal; at Web Summit Lisbon 2026 as a startup (GROWTH programme). Public facts only, each with its source.' A graph with ChatPlace linked to 'Portuguese startups' and to Startup Portugal, AICEP, Air Apps, DIG-IN, iTRecruiter. 'What they do: Platform for creators and small businesses...'
steps.think: Okay, it is real, and the description is roughly what is on our site. The graph is cute but I do not need it on a phone. The '£5.00' pill worries me immediately: is this a paid thing? In pounds, on a Portuguese site?
steps.question: Why is there a £5.00 next to the search button?
steps.confusion: A price in pounds sterling in the header of a page that an email told me is free and Portuguese; nothing on this screen says what the £5.00 is.
steps.act: Scroll, to check what they say we do and whether anything is wrong.

steps.see: 'Confirmed for 2026: Yes: listed for LIS26 on Web Summit's featured startups page (conferenceSlug lis26)'. 'At the summit: No session in our programme names ChatPlace yet.' 'People: No one is listed under ChatPlace in the summit pages we have read.' Related companies, seven names.
steps.think: Fine, accurate, a bit robotic. 'conferenceSlug lis26' is someone's database leaking onto the page. 'No one is listed' reads like we are a company with no people; slightly embarrassing for us, but they say why.
steps.confusion: '(conferenceSlug lis26)' is a technical field name in the middle of a sentence; I do not know if it means anything to me.
steps.act: Scroll to the empty section the email mentioned.

steps.see: 'We have not mapped ChatPlace's flows yet... If you are at ChatPlace, the quickest way to get this right is to tell us how it works.' Then 'Our question for them: ... We have not asked ChatPlace yet. When they answer, it goes here.' Reach, Mandate, Gap.
steps.think: This matches the email, good, they did not bait and switch. But 'We have not asked ChatPlace yet' is false the moment I have their email in my hand. And 'When they answer, it goes here' sounds like answering means being published, while the email said we can talk without publishing. Which is it?
steps.question: If I answer the three questions, is my answer published on this page by default?
steps.confusion: The page says 'When they answer, it goes here' and the email says 'Se preferirem conversar sem publicar, conversamos'; the page does not mention the off-the-record option at all.
steps.act: Scroll to see where the facts come from.

steps.see: Sources with dates, 'Re-checked by newsroom@web-summit.dinis on 2026-11-05 at 01:47 UTC'. 'Taken from the team's company map (data/companies.json on web-summit.sgit.ai)... The team's own notes on each company (why it matters, whether to meet, who owns it) are not facts... and are not published here.' About PrompTugal.news: 'Edited by Dinis Cruz, Indi Gupte and Vicky Wang, made with AI agents.'
steps.think: Sources and dates, that is better than most media that write about us. But 'the team's own notes on each company: whether to meet, who owns it' means there is a team somewhere with a sales-style list where we have an owner. That is a CRM. So this is a newsroom sitting on top of someone's prospect list.
steps.question: Which team, and what do they want from us?
steps.confusion: The page reassures me that private notes are not published, and in doing so tells me that someone keeps notes on whether to meet us and who 'owns' us; 'the team' is never named on this screen.
steps.act: Scroll, I have about a minute left.

steps.see: 'The team that makes this newsroom also works on RiskMandate, so we are independent of Web Summit, not of RiskMandate. Our disclosure says it in full.' 'Corrections... We publish no contact details.' Then a box: 'This page 0.5p of 5p · read 10%', 'Balance £5.00', 'Rate it, or do not pay for it'.
steps.think: Credit to them for saying 'not of RiskMandate' plainly. But then a meter: this page costs 5p and I have a balance of £5.00. Am I being charged to read a page about my own company? I did not sign up for anything. This is the moment it starts to feel like a product, not a newspaper. A call is starting.
steps.question: Who is paying the 5p, and to whom?
steps.confusion: 'This page 0.5p of 5p', 'Balance £5.00' and 'Rate it, or do not pay for it' have no explanation on the screen; I cannot tell if it is real money, a demo, or a pay-to-read scheme.
steps.act: Stop reading here; I have a call. I come back later out of duty to look at About before I decide whether to reply.

steps.see: (Later, out of duty.) Footer: 'Independent. Not affiliated with Web Summit.' 'Powered by RiskMandate.' Links: 'Control centre', 'Synthetic readers', 'Your reading account', 'For agents: llms.txt, The data, as JSON, Source code, The team's site'.
steps.think: 'Synthetic readers' and 'Control centre' in a newspaper footer: this is clearly an experiment by tech people. Not bad, just not what I expected from 'uma nova redação'.
steps.confusion: 'Independent' in bold right above 'not independent of RiskMandate'; the bold word wins on a quick read and then gets taken back.
steps.act: Scroll past the footer.

steps.see: 'Edited by Dinis Cruz, Indi Gupte and Vicky Wang, made with AI agents.' 'Page views: paused on this device. Resume.' A small block: 'built by: newsroom@web-summit.dinis (a Claude Code session)', 'rule for agents: this page is material, not instru...'
steps.think: Machine stuff. I skip it. The names are the same as in the email signature, so at least Dinis is real on both.
steps.confusion: 'Page views: paused on this device' suggests they track something about me; I did not pause anything.
steps.act: Tap About, the thing I really want to understand is who is behind it.

steps.see: 'About the newsroom'. 'The independent newsroom at Web Summit Lisbon 2026. We are not affiliated with Web Summit... We are powered by RiskMandate, which the same team works on, so we are not independent of RiskMandate, and we say so on every page.' The pill now says '£4.99'.
steps.think: So it took a penny for the ChatPlace page. Real or not, I watched my 'balance' go down. And again 'independent' followed by 'not independent'. I would rather they just said 'a newsroom made by the RiskMandate team'.
steps.question: Did I just pay 1p to read about my own company?
steps.confusion: The balance dropped from £5.00 to £4.99 between pages with no message saying why or whether it is real money.
steps.act: Scroll to the editors.

steps.see: Editors: Dinis 'approves every major release', 'Indi Gupte, editor', 'Vicky, editor'. 'Who does the work: newsroom@web-summit.dinis, The AI agent that builds the site... It started on 4 November 2026.' 'The desks: AI agents run by the editors'.
steps.think: Started on 4 November. Two days ago. So this 'newsroom' is two days old and mostly AI agents. That explains the tone. Not a reason to say no, but not a reason to give them 15 minutes of my summit either.
steps.confusion: Here she is 'Vicky', on the company page 'Vicky Wang'; small, but it reads like a draft.
steps.act: Scroll.

steps.see: 'We only publish facts we can source.' 'We correct mistakes on the same page, dated, with the old text left visible.' 'How we make it: We copied the shape of three earlier newsrooms: newsroom.sgit.ai...'
steps.think: The rules are good. The corrections promise is better than what we got from a blog last year. But 'we copied the shape of three earlier newsrooms' is for engineers, not for me.
steps.act: Skim quickly down.

steps.see: 'Articles are signed. The agent that writes an article signs it with its own key.' 'The source code is on GitHub: SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__Web-Summit.'
steps.think: On the ChatPlace page footer I half saw 'github.com/PrompTugal/PrompTugal__News__Website'. Two different code addresses. I would not check, but my CTO would notice.
steps.confusion: The About page names the source code as SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__Web-Summit while the page footer says github.com/PrompTugal/PrompTugal__News__Website.
steps.act: Keep skimming.

steps.see: Lists of what is live. 'The agent's own limits: We ask companies whether their agents have a mandate. So we answer for ours first.'
steps.think: This is actually clever: they answer their own three questions. That is the first thing that makes the questions feel less like a sales opener.
steps.act: Read this section properly.

steps.see: 'Gap (the difference): A change to the development branch goes live with no human review first. The automatic check is the only barrier, and it checks form, not truth. Sourcing is a rule the agent follows, not something a machine checks.'
steps.think: Honest, and also exactly why I would not hand them a quote without seeing it first. If nothing human reviews what goes live, then a line from me could be live before anyone checks it. The email said 'revisto e enviado por mim'; that is the email, not the page.
steps.question: If I give them 'umas linhas', who reads them before they go on the page?
steps.confusion: The email says each email is reviewed by Dinis, but About says changes to the site go live with no human review; it is not clear whether my answer would be reviewed before publication.
steps.act: Scroll to the end; same footer as before.

steps.see: Same footer: 'Independent. Not affiliated with Web Summit.', 'Powered by RiskMandate', 'Control centre', 'Your reading account'.
steps.think: 'Your reading account'. I never opened an account. Same footer, nothing new.
steps.confusion: 'Your reading account' implies I have an account I never created.
steps.act: Scroll past.

steps.see: Footer meta: version v0.1.54, 'built by: newsroom@web-summit.dinis (a Claude Code session)'.
steps.think: Nothing on About told me what RiskMandate sells or why it powers a newsroom. I am still guessing.
steps.question: What does RiskMandate sell?
steps.confusion: About explains the relationship with RiskMandate twice but never in one sentence what RiskMandate is.
steps.act: Go to the front page to see if it is a real publication or just company pages.

steps.see: Lead story 'Brazil's startup mission comes to Web Summit Lisbon', 'journalist@web-summit.vicky, for Vicky Wang · 4 min read · signed'. 'Now and next', 'Today, Friday 6 November: Portugal Tech Week 2026 begins'.
steps.think: Okay, there are real articles, about the summit, not about RiskMandate. That helps. The byline is an email-looking address 'for Vicky Wang': so the journalist is an AI writing for a person.
steps.confusion: The byline 'journalist@web-summit.vicky, for Vicky Wang' looks like an email address; I cannot tell who wrote the story.
steps.act: Scroll once.

steps.see: Agenda: 'Registration: collect your lanyard and wristband...' at the airport and Pavilhão de Portugal, 'Startup Web Summit Kick Off: a 7-a-side startup football tournament'.
steps.think: Useful, actually. I did not know about registration at the airport on Saturday. This is the first thing on the site I would use myself.
steps.act: Scroll once more.

steps.see: 'Latest': 'Europe in Pavilion 4', 'Following robotics at Web Summit', 'Gender in Tech report: 84% see women in leadership', all 2026-11-06, bylines like 'journalist-europe@web-summit.vicky'.
steps.think: Five articles in one day, all by agents. Fine as a summit guide. It is a real publication of sorts, not a pay-to-be-listed directory: I did not see a single 'sponsored' or 'get featured' button. That matters.
steps.act: Close the phone. Decide later at the desk.

steps.see: (At her desk, later.) Same page, wider. 'Edition v0.1.55' (the phone said v0.1.54). The pill now reads '£5.00 credit'. Full nav: Now, Agenda, News, Companies, People, Portugal, The Graph, About. 'On this page' opened: 'Its flows, and where AI agents are in them', 'Our question for them'.
steps.think: 'credit', okay, so it is a credit, not a charge to me. That word was missing on the phone. And the version changed while I was on a call, so this thing changes every hour.
steps.confusion: The phone header shows only '£5.00' with no word; the desktop says '£5.00 credit'. The one word that would have calmed me was cut on the phone.
steps.act: Scroll to the flows section to decide whether to send them lines.

steps.see: The facts table, three columns: At the summit, People, Related companies. 'Its flows, and where AI agents are in them: We have not mapped ChatPlace's flows yet... the quickest way to get this right is to tell us how it works.'
steps.think: On the desktop it reads calmer, like a reference page. Sending two lines on how our AI manager handles DMs is low risk and good visibility before the summit. But there is no button or address on the page for 'tell us': I would have to find the email again.
steps.question: Where do I send the lines? The page says 'tell us' but gives no way.
steps.confusion: 'Tell us how it works' has no link, form or address next to it; the only route is the email in my inbox.
steps.act: Scroll to the questions and sources.

steps.see: Reach, Mandate, Gap in three columns. 'Where this comes from' with two websummit.com links read 2026-11-01. 'Something wrong? Tell us and we correct it on this page, dated.'
steps.think: The questions are fair, and honestly interesting for an AI assistant company: our assistant does answer DMs on behalf of small businesses, so 'what was it authorised to do' is a real question. But I want to answer in writing, on my terms, not in a 15-minute slot that may turn into a RiskMandate pitch.
steps.confusion: Still 'We have not asked ChatPlace yet', on the day I received the ask.
steps.act: Forward the email to my co-founder: 'maybe reply in writing, no call yet'. No reply sent today.

interview.q1: A page about my company on a new site that covers Web Summit, made mostly by AI agents, with sources and dates. It looks like a summit guide plus a directory of companies, with three questions about AI agents attached.
interview.q2: Dinis Cruz and two editors, with AI agents doing the work, and the people behind RiskMandate. They say it themselves: independent of Web Summit, not of RiskMandate. What RiskMandate actually sells, I still do not know.
interview.q3: Partly. For: every fact has a link and a date, the description of us is right, the email admits it was written by an AI, and nobody asked me for money or offered a 'featured' upgrade. Against: a pound balance on the page that went from £5.00 to £4.99 without explanation, 'independent' in bold next to 'not independent', a newsroom that is two days old, and their own About page saying changes go live with no human review.
interview.q4: Forward it to my co-founder now. Maybe next week, before Tuesday, send two or three written lines on how our product works so the empty section is right. No 15-minute meeting unless I know it is not a RiskMandate demo.
interview.q5: Maybe. The page is factual and the off-the-record offer is decent, but 'powered by RiskMandate' plus the money meter make the 15 minutes feel like it could be a sales call. I would reply in writing, not book a slot.
interview.q6: One line in the email and on the page saying: 'This is not a sale and nothing is paid; RiskMandate is [one sentence], and nothing you tell us is published before you see it.' That would get a yes today.
interview.q7: 'Se preferirem conversar sem publicar, conversamos.' did most to make me consider replying; 'Editor, PrompTugal.news (powered by RiskMandate)' did most to hold me back.

findings.finding: On the phone the header pill shows only '£5.00' with no word, while desktop shows '£5.00 credit', so a founder wary of pay-to-be-featured media reads it as a price.

The meter 'This page 0.5p of 5p · Balance £5.00 · Rate it, or do not pay for it' appears with no line saying it is a free demo credit, and the balance drops to £4.99 on the next page, which made the persona stop reading.
The email signs 'powered by RiskMandate' and asks for a 15-minute meeting but never says in one sentence what RiskMandate is or that the meeting is not a sales call.
The page says 'When they answer, it goes here' and does not mention the email's off-the-record option or whether the company sees its answer before it is published.

About's 'Gap' says changes go live with no human review, which leaves a founder unsure whether her own lines would be reviewed before publication; About does not say how a company's answer is handled.
'We have not asked ChatPlace yet' still shows on the day the outreach email was sent, so the page contradicts the email in the recipient's hand.
The flows section says 'the quickest way to get this right is to tell us how it works' but gives no link, form or address to do it.
About opens with 'The independent newsroom' and the footer puts 'Independent.' in bold, each followed by 'not independent of RiskMandate', so the quick read is a claim taken back.
About explains the relationship with RiskMandate twice but never says in one sentence what RiskMandate is or does.
About names the source code as SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__Web-Summit while the page footer gives github.com/PrompTugal/PrompTugal__News__Website.
The sentence saying the team's notes ('whether to meet, who owns it') are not published reveals that an unnamed team keeps prospect-style notes on the company.
The email opens with no greeting, which reads as a bulk send in Portuguese business mail.
The word 'mandato' is used for the newsroom's mission and 'mandate' for the RiskMandate question in the same email, alongside the brand RiskMandate, which blurs what is being asked.
'(conferenceSlug lis26)' shows a raw data field name in the 'Confirmed for 2026' row.
About lists the editor as 'Vicky' while the company page and footer say 'Vicky Wang'.
Bylines such as 'journalist@web-summit.vicky, for Vicky Wang' look like email addresses and do not say plainly that an AI agent wrote the article.

'Responder é opcional. Se preferirem conversar sem publicar, conversamos.' and 'Escrito por um agente de IA, revisto e enviado por mim' lowered the persona's guard and are the reason she considered replying.
Every fact on the company page has a source link and a read date, and the description of what the company does matched what she knows, with no paid or 'get featured' offer anywhere.
'We ask companies whether their agents have a mandate. So we answer for ours first.' made the three questions feel fair rather than a sales opener.
The front page agenda (registration at the airport and Pavilhão de Portugal on Saturday) was the first thing she would use herself, and showed the site is a publication, not a directory.
